Uninsured rental detection and automatic re-bind

Insurance drift alerting via reminders row + in-app bell

Per-run time budget so the isolate is never killed mid-repair; leftovers roll to the next tick
Rationale: ABI has no webhooks, no idempotency keys, answers failures with {} — the cron IS the integration's correctness mechanism
Rationale: no bespoke X-Cron-Secret — net.http_post is async so a 401 would never surface in cron.job_run_details and the loop would look healthy
Rationale: ABI sends local wall clock + TIMEZONE, never an instant — treating it as UTC moves end-of-cover by up to twelve hours
Rationale: join key compared at MINUTE precision because ABI returns HH:mm while we send HH:mm:ss — string equality would report every coverage missing
Rationale: abort the tenant if listRentals fails — an empty list from a failed call is indistinguishable from an empty policy and would mark every coverage uninsured
Rationale: raiseAlert is contractually incapable of throwing — an alert that breaks its own repair turns a recoverable uninsured rental into an unrecoverable one
Rationale: ux_reminders_identity is UNIQUE on (rule_code,object_type,object_id,due_on,remind_on) — read first then upsert so the repeat count survives and 23505 is avoided
Rationale: ABI will not backdate cover — a repair for a live rental starts now and the gap that already happened cannot be bought back
Rationale: attemptRebind deliberately does not call addRenter — duplicating renter mapping would give two places that decide what a valid renter looks like
Rationale: mock tenants excluded from the cron (mock transport returns an empty list so every coverage reads uninsured); includeMock deliberately drives that path as the credential-free test
Rationale: EXTERNALREF is write-only at ABI so VIN + start-time overlap is the only attribution available; ambiguity means do nothing rather than attach cover to the wrong rental
Rationale: one tenant's failure must never stop the others — the next tenant may be the one with an uninsured car on the road
Monthly INSHUR vendor cost sync into per-vehicle P&L
Query-param casing probe with tenant-level override persistence
Billed-vs-covered VIN variance reporting and unowned-VIN escalation
Billing alerting via reminders row + in-app bell (second copy of the reconciler's raiseAlert)
Previous-whole-calendar-month billing window, run on the 3rd so the vendor has closed the month

Rationale: the proposed inshur_billing_lines table was never applied, so vendor cost lands in vehicle_expenses — without it the operator's whole INSHUR spend is invisible in P&L while rental revenue counts, overstating per-vehicle margin
Rationale: API reference says ?STARTDATE= and our 2026-05-23 discovery doc says ?startDate= — a wrong guess silently returns the whole history or nothing, i.e. silently wrong money
Rationale: an empty month resolves nothing and is reported inconclusive — recording it would pin the wrong spelling on the strength of no evidence
Rationale: a manual casing pin is an operator's explicit statement about the vendor API and outranks anything we could infer
Rationale: mock tenants excluded with no override — synthesising cost figures would put invented money into the operator's P&L
Rationale: start/end_time_sent are 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' strings so lexicographic comparison is chronological; overlap not containment so a straddling rental is billed in this period too
Rationale: deterministic expense reference inshur-{start}-{end}-{vin} makes re-running a month a no-op
Rationale: expense_category has no Insurance member, so category='Other' and the vendor column carries the real classification; the P&L trigger maps Other to Expenses
Rationale: one narrow local fetch duplicates inshur-client's transport because the shared client hardcodes the documented path and resolving the casing must not require a redeploy
INSHUR credential smoke test for the Settings panel
states-allowed endpoint path probe with override persistence
Covered-states cache feeding the go-live preflight and out-of-area booking rejection
Only head_admin/admin (or super admin) may exercise ABI credentials
Inline-value-wins credential resolution, trimmed so one pasted leading space cannot silently break every later auth
Rationale: verifies the credentials it is HANDED, not the tenant row — a mock-mode tenant pasting live credentials would otherwise have them 'verified' against a simulator that passes any input
Rationale: covered-states is a blocking go-live gate, so a wrong endpoint guess would lock go-live permanently with no UI escape — hence probing both candidates and storing the winner
Rationale: every verification OUTCOME is HTTP 200 with ok:false — supabase-js buries a non-2xx body inside FunctionsHttpError where the panel cannot render mode/runtimeAllowsLive
Rationale: INSHUR_ALLOW_LIVE is opt-OUT — an unset secret that forbade live mode would make the go-live preflight unsatisfiable from the UI
Rationale: only wrong-URL-shaped failures justify the alternate path — retrying an auth rejection walks the account towards lockout and retrying a timeout doubles the operator's wait
Rationale: raw ABI GET duplicated from _shared/inshur-client.ts because the client hardcodes one path per operation and probing multiple paths is this function's whole reason for existing

Rationale: callerOrigin is honoured only when it is not localhost — a real customer's reminder email must never land back on a host they cannot resolve
Rationale: verify the saved Stripe customer still exists and fall back to a customer-less session keyed by email — mock/seeded plans and deleted Stripe data must not crash the link
Rationale: the token records last_used_session_id but stays reusable until paid, so a bounced or abandoned checkout does not strand the customer

Rationale: plan deletion blocks on anything NOT terminal (only canceled/incomplete_expired allowed) — 'incomplete' and 'unpaid' come back LIVE and nothing ever restores plan_id, so an unrecognised future Stripe status must block loudly

Rationale: delete the row first and archive the Stripe price after — the FK is ON DELETE SET NULL so history release is atomic, and archiving ahead of a failed delete would leave a plan advertised that checkout cannot use
Rationale: a Stripe price that no longer exists cannot bill anyone, so a resource_missing error must never block deactivating or deleting the plan row
Rationale: super-admin check also requires is_active — cross-referenced to the note in mark-invoice-paid

Rationale: set VoiceUrl directly on the number, never VoiceApplicationSid — the TwiML App's VoiceUrl is the OUTBOUND handler and would route real inbound calls through it
Rationale: the preview re-invokes the real twilio-voice-inbound with Preview=1 so there is zero logic drift between what is previewed and what callers get
Rationale: twilio-voice-inbound always self-returns 200 even for its error TwiML, so a non-200 here is a gateway failure and its body must not be handed back as 'twiml'
Rationale: test-forward-call places a real, billed call on the tenant's own Twilio account, so it requires an explicit confirm:true

Rationale: Stripe is the authority and reconcile-subscriptions rewrites the DB from it, so a hand-edited status row is reverted within the hour while the tenant is still dunned — hence stripe.invoices.pay({paid_out_of_band}) and convergence via the invoice.paid webhook
Rationale: app_users has its own primary key and links to auth via auth_user_id — matching on id silently matches nothing (verified zero of 48 rows) and would reject every super admin
Rationale: is_active is checked too — without it a deactivated super admin kept the ability to mark platform invoices paid, rewrite plans, start migrations and delete tenants

Rationale: a hard migration blocker is not dismissible, so a call for a hard-blocked tenant is rejected rather than silently honoured
